Whitelists: Implement a whitelist mechanism to allow only authorized addresses to interact with the contract. This can be managed by the contract owner or through a governance system where token holders vote to whitelist certain addresses.

CAPTCHA or Proof of Work: Integrate CAPTCHA challenges or proof-of-work puzzles into your contract interaction process. This can deter automated bots, as solving these challenges requires human intervention and computational resources.

Gas Price Limit: Set a gas price limit to prevent front-running attacks. Bots often exploit price differences during network congestion by paying higher gas fees. Enforcing a maximum gas price can prevent such attacks.

Rate Limiting: Implement rate limits on contract interactions. Limit the number of transactions a single address can make within a specific timeframe. This prevents bots from overwhelming the contract with rapid transactions.

Dynamic Fees: Implement dynamic transaction fees based on the frequency of transactions from an address. Higher fees can be imposed on addresses that frequently interact with the contract, making it economically unfeasible for bots to exploit.

In this case, trades will receive sub-optimal rates, and if no liquidity provider is

lling to rectify the situation, the pair is stuck. sync() exists to set the reserves of the contract to the current balances, providing a somewhat graceful recovery from this situation.skim() functions as a recovery mechanism in case enough tokens are sent to an pair to overflow the two uint112 storage slots for reserves, which could otherwise cause trades to fail. skim() allows a user to withdraw the difference between the cur
t balance of the pair and 2112 − 1 to the caller, if that difference is greater than 0.
